fact: On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed the digital transformation ministry's draft bills, including a data and artificial intelligence bill, and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament, a joint sitting of the Sovereignty and Ministers councils; the article does not describe the bill's content.

The Data Protection Africa factsheet states Sudan has no data protection law and no data protection authority appointed; the date is the page's last-updated stamp, 24 May 2022, and parts of the text may be older.
The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 2023-03-15 and had not ratified it.

The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says Sudan has no privacy law or legal framework governing personal data, and that a 2018 draft data protection bill was never enacted; no date of its own is given, so the published date of 2026-07-19 is used.

The article states Sudan is a signatory to the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention), which it says has been in force since 2023, and that Sudan has yet to enact or implement it; no signing date is given, so the published date of 2026-07-19 is used.

The article says that as of mid-2026 neither the Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority nor the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority, both established by a November 2025 decree, has issued binding rules, citing the AI Regulation Tracker.
